findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing originating from west side of property but no specific label for "Point of Service" or "POS"; the connection point is shown but not explicitly designated as the POS per AE Design requirements. Sheet 9 shows a single transformer pad but no POS designation. Sheet 31 shows only overhead electric line on boundary, no POS marked. The point of service location and primary source location are not clearly labeled or designated on any of the required plan sheets.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) requires the point of electric service to be shown on plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements. While Sheet 21 shows electrical infrastructure and apparent connection points, these are not explicitly labeled as the "Point of Service" or identified as the location where Austin Energy's and the customer's conductors connect. Per UCM § 1.3.4, the POS is the specific location of connection or termination. The absence of explicit POS designation on required sheets (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) means the POS location cannot be verified as shown per code requirements. On Sheet 21, while the general routing is shown, the specific POS is not called out.
findings.comment: Point of electric service (POS) location is not explicitly designated on required plan sheets. Add clear labeling of the point of service location (meter socket, pedestal, pull-box, or AE-designated enclosure) on all required sheets per UCM § 1.16.0(6) and UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows complete underground electric line routing from street entry point through site with conduit paths and connection to pull boxes and meters. Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) shows water (-W-), sanitary sewer (-WW-), and storm drain (-SD-) routing, but does NOT show underground electric line routing despite electric infrastructure being shown elsewhere on the site plan (one transformer pad noted). Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows only overhead electric (OHE) on the boundary, with no underground conduit or cable routing depicted. Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) includes electrical symbols in the legend (-E- for Proposed Underground Electric) but contains NO actual underground electric lines drawn on the plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires underground electric cabling routing and service lines to be shown on required plan sheets including site plan showing all utilities, landscape plan, and all electrical plans. The inconsistency across sheets violates this requirement. While detailed electrical routing is shown on the dedicated Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), the required plan sheets per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B (Site Plan and Landscape Plan) do not show this infrastructure. The absence of underground electric routing on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) is particularly significant, as this sheet shows other underground utilities (water, sewer, storm) in detail but omits electrical routing. Similarly, the Utility Tap Plan (Sheet 19) shows a legend entry for proposed underground electric but draws no such lines, creating an incomplete utility coordination drawing.
findings.comment: Underground electric conduit routing and service lines must be shown on all required plan sheets including site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31). Add underground electric line routing showing connections from property line source through site to service connection points per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 5 transformer pads with specific locations labeled (near northwest entrance, west of Bldg 2, east of Bldg 4, west of Bldg 8, east of Bldg 7). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows one transformer pad labeled as "Transformer Pad (Typ.)" on the west side near Building 1. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show any transformer pads, transformer locations, or transformer equipment - no symbols or labels for transformers are visible on this sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B requires all electrical plans to be included in the plan set, and Table 1.4.3.A specifies that Electric UG Transformers and Electric OH Transformers must appear on CAD layers. While transformers are shown on the dedicated Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21), they must also be shown on the required sheets specified in Table 1.4.3.B, including the landscape plan per the code's requirement to show electric infrastructure on all required sheets. The absence of transformer locations on Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means the landscape designer has not coordinated around the electrical transformer equipment, creating a potential conflict between landscaping and electrical infrastructure placement.
findings.comment: Transformer pad locations must be shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9). Show all transformer pad locations with corresponding labels to ensure proper coordination with landscape design and site layout per UCM § 1.4.2.6.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) clearly shows 8 electrical meter locations, labeled "Electrical Meters" at specific building locations (north wall of Bldg 1, north wall of Bldg 3, east wall of Bldg 5, south wall of Bldg 2, south wall of Bldg 4, east wall of Bldg 6, south wall of Bldg 7, south wall of Bldg 8). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does NOT show any electrical meter locations - despite showing other utilities (water, sewer, storm) and one transformer pad. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does NOT show any electrical meter locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.4 defines the Point of Service and requires its location to be shown. The electrical meter locations are critical to identifying the customer's service equipment and POS. UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires all electrical plans and the site plan showing all utilities and landscape plan to include electric infrastructure. The absence of meter locations on Sheet 9 (Site Plan showing all utilities) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) means these required sheets do not show the complete electric service infrastructure. The customer's service equipment (meters) must be shown on all required plan sheets for proper utility coordination and to verify POS compliance.
findings.comment: Electric meter locations must be shown on site plan showing all utilities (Sheet 9) and landscape plan (Sheet 31) in addition to the electrical plan. Add labels identifying the location and number of electrical meters serving each building per UCM § 1.3.4.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 electrical plan which shows underground electric service with standard service lateral conduit routing to each building. The electrical routing appears to show typical service-only conduit sizes (not the 1000 MCM cables in 5-inch conduit that would indicate main line distribution). No Austin Energy ESPA documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes are provided in the supplementary documents that would indicate whether duct banks are required for this project. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Austin Energy design criteria but the actual AE comments are on an external Bluebeam link that cannot be accessed for this review.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item notes this determination "cannot be determined from plans alone" and requires checking Austin Energy ESPA documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes indicating duct bank infrastructure. Sheet 21 shows what appears to be service-only routing, but without formal AE Design documentation confirming that duct banks are NOT required, the requirement cannot be definitively verified. The absence of AE Design approval documentation in the project file means the applicant may have received AE determinations that are not available in this document set. This determination requires confirmation from Austin Energy as referenced in the grouping's regulatory overview.
findings.comment: Cannot verify whether duct bank routing and locations are required for this project from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval letter, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes confirming whether main line duct banks are required or service-only routing is approved.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) were examined for street lighting layout and light pole locations. Sheet 9 includes a Lighting Note addressing "exterior lighting" (building wall-mounted lights), not street lighting infrastructure. No street lighting, light poles, or photometric layouts are shown on either sheet. Facts.md indicates Valley View Road is classified as a local street (ASMP Level 1) with existing lane count not on file and a 2-undivided-lane cross-section planned. The site plan does not show street improvements along Valley View Road frontage that would typically trigger street lighting requirements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.6.0 requires street lighting to be shown when required, and the grouping notes state to "Check: Site plan for street frontage and street improvement requirements; contact AE Design business unit for street lighting determination." The absence of explicit street improvement requirements on Valley View Road frontage and the absence of street lighting from the plans suggest it may not be required. However, the determination cannot be made from site plan review alone per UCM § 1.6.0 - it requires direct contact with AE Design. The checklist item states this determination "cannot be determined from plans alone" and must be verified through AE Design coordination, which does not appear to have been completed or documented.
findings.comment: Cannot verify whether street lighting is required for this site from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required for the Valley View Road frontage per UCM § 1.6.0. If required, show street light layout and pole locations on site plan and landscape plan.

findings.observation: No street light conduit, conduit connections, or conduit routing are shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan), or Sheet 21 (Electrical Plan). As noted in EL-17.7 findings, street lighting infrastructure is not visible anywhere in the plan set. The applicability of this item depends on whether street lighting is required, which per UCM § 1.6.0 must be determined by contacting Austin Energy Design.
findings.reasoning: Per the checklist item's applicability note, this item applies "Only when street lighting or parking garage lighting is required." The grouping's regulatory overview (Section 8 of grouping file) states: "Specific street lighting requirements are determined by contacting AE Design (UCM § 1.6.0)." Without documentation of AE Design's determination regarding street lighting applicability, this item's applicability cannot be confirmed. If street lighting is determined to be required by AE Design, then the absence of street light conduit plans would be a deficiency.
findings.comment: Cannot determine applicability from available evidence. Clarify with Austin Energy Design whether street lighting is required. If required, provide street light conduit plan showing conduit connections and routing on site plan, landscape plan, and all electrical plans per UCM § 1.6.0.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan). No electrical load calculations, demand summaries, amperage requirements, voltage specifications, or load data appear on any of these sheets. No tables or callouts showing projected electrical load for the development (e.g., total kW, total amps, demand load per building) are present. The sheets show physical infrastructure (transformers, meters, lines) but do not quantify the electrical service demand.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(6) explicitly requires the projected electrical load to be shown on plan sheets. This is critical information for Austin Energy to determine service capacity, transformer sizing, and whether line extensions or additional infrastructure are required. The grouping's common violation patterns (item 6 in Description section) lists "Missing projected load: No indication of projected electrical load for the development" as a violation. The absence of load data on any plan sheet prevents verification of service adequacy and AE Design determination of infrastructure requirements.
findings.comment: Projected electrical load must be shown on plan sheets. Add load calculations table to the electrical design plan showing total projected electrical demand in kW and/or amperes, and breakdown by building if applicable, per UCM § 1.16.0(6).

findings.observation: This is a master planned development with 39 townhome units across 8 buildings in a unified site plan, but it is not a multi-lot subdivision with separate lot development phases. The single site plan shows all proposed buildings and infrastructure in one development. No separate master electrical plan from the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) consultant is provided in the supplementary documents or referenced in the plan set. The applicability note states "Only for master planned developments with multiple lots" - the interpretation of whether this unified multi-building development triggers the master plan requirement is ambiguous.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item's applicability language states "Only for master planned developments with multiple lots." This site is a single unified development of 39 units in 8 buildings, not a platted subdivision with separate lots held by different owners. However, the phrase "master planned development" could potentially include any large multi-building development. The grouping does not define this term precisely. Without a clear definition distinguishing single-site multi-building developments from true master planned multi-lot subdivisions, the applicability cannot be definitively determined. If this project type is intended to require a separate master plan from an MEP consultant, that requirement should be clarified.
findings.comment: Clarify whether a separate Master Electrical Plan from the MEP consultant is required for this multi-building residential development. If required, provide the master electrical plan showing loads for all buildings and service routing strategy per Reviewer Convention.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows transformer pads (5 total) but no indication of vault structures. The facts.md indicates the site is located in Austin, TX but does NOT place it within the Downtown Network Area per facts.md statement "Regulating Plan: None". UCM § 1.11.5 defines the Network Area boundaries where vaults are permitted. The applicability note in the checklist states vaults are required only "Inside Network Area: vaults required for services above 800 amps. Outside Network Area: vaults generally not permitted - only pad-mounted transformers or specialized niches." The site appears to be outside the Network Area, suggesting pad-mounted transformers (which are shown) would be the appropriate service type. However, without formal Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the service type decision and demonstrating compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 (Clearances from AE Padmount Equipment) if pedestals/niches are used, the determination cannot be conclusively verified.
findings.reasoning: The determination of whether vaults are required cannot be made from site plan features alone - it requires (1) confirmation of location relative to Network Area boundaries, and (2) Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the approved service type. While the site appears to be outside the Network Area (suggesting pad-mounted transformers are appropriate), formal AE Design documentation is required to verify this determination. The absence of such documentation means the applicant's choice of pad-mounted transformers cannot be verified as AE-approved.
findings.comment: Cannot verify vault requirements from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy Design documentation (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes) confirming the approved service type (pad-mounted transformer, vault, or specialized niche). If pad-mounted transformers are approved, verify compliance with UCM § 1.10.4 clearance requirements per UCM § 1.5.1.6.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 electrical meter locations labeled "Electrical Meters" but does not specify whether these are pedestal-mounted service equipment or other enclosure types. The site plan shows pad-mounted transformers with underground service to meter locations, but the specific meter enclosure type is not detailed. No Austin Energy Design documentation (ESPA approval, Letter of Agreement, utility coordination notes) is provided confirming whether pedestals are the approved service type for this project. UCM § 1.5.3.4 notes pedestals are typically used for residential services up to 200 amps maximum.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item's applicability note states: "Check: Austin Energy Design documentation, Letter of Agreement, or utility coordination notes specifying pedestal service." The absence of this documentation means the service type (whether pedestals are required/approved) cannot be verified from site plan review alone. While the physical location of meters is shown, their enclosure type (pedestal vs. other) is not specified on the drawings.
findings.comment: Cannot verify whether electrical service pedestals are required from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy Design documentation confirming the approved service type and equipment enclosure specification (pedestal, meter socket, service distribution enclosure, or other AE-approved enclosure) per UCM § 1.5.3.4.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric service is required (indicated by "Underground Electric Line" routing and underground conduit to all buildings). However, no trenching assignments are shown on the plans. No notes or callouts indicate which party (customer vs. contractor) is responsible for trenching work, no depth specifications are provided, no existing utility conflict avoidance strategy is shown, and no trenching sequence is documented. This is in contrast to water and wastewater utility notes on other sheets which specify material sizing and installation standards.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.3.4 states "Customer responsible for trenching per UCM § 1.5.3.4, but specific plan documentation requirement is operational practice." While the code makes the customer responsible, the plan documentation of this responsibility and associated requirements (depths, conflicts, sequencing) is standard practice for underground utility projects. The absence of trenching assignments on the electrical plan creates ambiguity regarding customer obligations for installing the conduit and cables.
findings.comment: Add trenching assignment notes to the electrical design plan. Clearly identify the customer's trenching responsibilities, including trench depth, locating and avoiding existing utilities, and any special constraints per UCM § 1.5.3.4 and standard construction practice for underground electric service.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and the Engineer's Summary Letter. No gas service infrastructure is shown on any electrical or site planning documents. No notes indicate whether gas service is required or planned for the development. The Engineer's Summary Letter (supplementary-docs/engineer-s-summary-letter) discusses water and wastewater utilities in detail but makes no mention of gas service requirements or determination. No notation indicates which buildings (if any) will use gas service, nor is there any statement that gas service is not required.
findings.reasoning: This is a Reviewer Convention item applicable to all sites. While natural gas is not always required, best practice dictates that plans should indicate whether gas service will be used or is not applicable to the development. The absence of any reference to gas service on plans or in project documentation creates ambiguity - it is unclear whether gas service was considered and determined unnecessary, or whether the requirement was overlooked. For a residential development with 39 units, gas service determination is a material utility planning item.
findings.comment: Add a note to the site plan or utility plan clarifying whether natural gas service is required for the development. If gas service is required, show routing and service connection details. If gas service is not required, add a note stating "Gas service not required for this development" per Reviewer Convention.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric service routing from the existing right-of-way at Valley View Road to the site, with connection to transformer pads and building meter locations. However, no documentation indicates whether this represents a "Line Extension" (customer-paid infrastructure extension to reach the site) or a "Service-Only" connection to existing nearby infrastructure. No terms such as "line extension," "CIAC" (Contribution in Aid of Construction), or "service-only" appear on the plans. The Master Comment Report's Electric Review section references Austin Energy Design Criteria but the actual AE Design determination (via ESPA approval or Letter of Agreement) is not provided in the project file.
findings.reasoning: The grouping's regulatory overview states: "Whether line extension is required (vs. Service-Only service) cannot be determined from site plan features alone - this determination is made by AE Design based on existing infrastructure capacity and location." The checklist item applicability note directs reviewers to: "Check: Austin Energy ESPA approval letters, Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service, or utility coordination notes stating line extension requirement and costs." The absence of this critical AE Design documentation means line extension applicability cannot be verified from available evidence.
findings.comment: Cannot verify whether electric line extension is required from available evidence. Provide Austin Energy ESPA approval letter or Letter of Agreement for Underground Electric Service confirming whether line extension is required and, if so, showing the extent of the line extension on the electrical design plan per UCM § 1.3.12 and UCM § 1.16.0(6).

findings.observation: Sheet 21 is titled "Preliminary Electrical Design Plan" and shows a site plan view with electrical infrastructure (transformer pads, meters, underground conduit, pull boxes, overhead facilities). However, it is unclear whether this sheet constitutes a formal "Electric Site Plan" submittal as required by UCM § 1.4.2.6, or whether a more comprehensive separate "Electric Site Plan" document is required from a licensed professional engineer. The grouping's applicability note states: "Check: Project complexity, Austin Energy coordination notes, and submittal requirements for the development type." No documentation clarifies whether the included Sheet 21 satisfies the requirement or if a separate, more detailed Electric Site Plan is needed.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item's applicability depends on project complexity and specific submittal requirements. The inclusion of "Preliminary" in the sheet title raises the question of whether this is a final electrical plan or a preliminary design that will be superseded by a more detailed separate submittal. Without clear documentation of submittal requirements for this development type or confirmation from Austin Energy that Sheet 21 satisfies the Electric Site Plan requirement, the item's applicability cannot be definitively determined.
findings.comment: Clarify whether Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) constitutes the required Electric Site Plan per UCM § 1.4.2.6, or whether a separate detailed Electric Site Plan from a licensed professional engineer is required. If a separate submittal is required, provide it as a separate document per Reviewer Convention.

findings.observation: Examined the primary site plan (39 sheets) per the README.md. No One-Line Diagram (also called Riser Diagram or Single-Line Diagram) of the electrical service is included in any of the 39 sheets. Checked Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) which would be the most likely location - it contains site plan view of physical infrastructure but no one-line diagram showing electrical service configuration, voltage, phases, breaker sizes, load distribution, or riser details. No supplementary document titled "One-Line Diagram" or "Electrical Riser Diagram" appears in the supplementary documents list in README.md.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B explicitly lists "One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser" as a required hardcopy plan for all sites. A one-line (or single-line) diagram is a fundamental electrical design document showing the connection schematic of the electrical service, not a physical site plan view. The absence of this document from the plan set is a direct violation of the code requirement. While Sheet 21 shows physical infrastructure locations, it does not include the schematic electrical diagram required by the code.
findings.comment: Provide One-Line Diagram of the electrical riser showing electrical service configuration, voltage, phases, main breaker, load calculations, and service routing strategy per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.B. This is a required plan sheet for all sites.

findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 9 (Site Plan), and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) for clearance dimensions between electrical facilities and other structures. No dimension callouts or clearance notes are shown between transformer pads and buildings, between overhead electric lines and buildings/structures, between underground conduit and other utilities, or between electrical equipment and landscaping. No clearance specifications per UCM § 1.10.3 (Clearances from AE Overhead Lines) or UCM § 1.10.4 (Clearances from AE Padmount Equipment) are noted on any sheet.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0(2) requires plans to demonstrate sufficient clearances for existing and proposed electric facilities. This is critical for safety, maintenance, and code compliance. The absence of clearance dimensions or specifications creates uncertainty about whether electrical facilities meet minimum setback requirements from buildings, other utilities, and landscaping. While the infrastructure is shown, the clearances are not demonstrated through dimensional callouts or specification notes.
findings.comment: Add clearance dimensions to all plan sheets showing sufficient clearances between electrical facilities (transformers, meters, conduit, overhead lines) and buildings, other utilities, and landscaping per UCM § 1.16.0(2). Provide dimensions per UCM § 1.10.3 (overhead clearances) and UCM § 1.10.4 (padmount equipment clearances).

findings.observation: No CAD files or information about CAD file georeferencing are provided in the project documentation or supplementary documents. The README.md lists primary site plan sheets and supplementary documents but does not indicate whether native CAD files are available for review or whether they have been verified as georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 per UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements. The site plan sheets show a scale (1" = 20') and benchmarks but do not explicitly state the coordinate system or contain information about CAD layer assignments and colors (Magenta for electrical layers per Table 1.4.3.A).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires CAD files to be georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 and specifies required layer names and colors (all electric infrastructure in Magenta: Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. Pole, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. MH). Without access to the native CAD files or documentation of their georeferencing, this requirement cannot be verified. Site plan sheets do not contain CAD layer information or coordinate system documentation.
findings.comment: Cannot verify CAD file georeferencing from available evidence. Provide certification that the CAD file is georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 per UCM § 1.4.2.6, and verify that all electric infrastructure elements are assigned to required Magenta layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. Pole, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. MH) per UCM § 1.4.2.6 Table 1.4.3.A.
